channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: United Kingdom: Services-led growth and price risks – Nomura
item.description: Nomura’s European Economics team highlights that UK composite output PMI rose to 52.5 in August, with services offsetting weaker manufacturing. GfK consumer confidence improved to its highest level in two years, supporting activity.

item.title: EUR/GBP slips as strong PMIs cancel out and Iran signals de-escalation
item.description: The Euro (EUR) is falling against the British Pound (GBP). EUR/GBP held the mid-0.8500s on Friday, hovering just below the 0.8570 area, even after a strong round of August flash Purchasing Managers Indexes (PMIs) on both sides of the cross.

item.title: US Dollar: Jackson Hole volatility over credibility – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities strategists argue that Kevin Warsh’s Jackson Hole speech will focus on structural themes such as productivity, AI-driven growth and Federal Reserve (Fed) regime change.

item.title: Euro: PMI strength supports against US Dollar – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s (BBH) Elias Haddad reports EUR/USD is firmer on broad US Dollar (USD) weakness and stronger-than-expected Eurozone August Purchasing Managers' Index (PMI) data. Elias Haddad highlights the composite PMI at a nine-month high, driven by manufacturing.

item.title: Japanese Yen strengthens against US Dollar as inflation backs BoJ rate hike bets
item.description: USD/JPY trades around 158.85 on Friday at the time of writing, edging lower after rebounding from the 158.00 level on Thursday.

item.title: $4,600: Gold rallies to three-month high, eyes third weekly gain
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) consolidates its intraday advance during American trading hours on Friday after briefly climbing above $4,600 earlier in the day, its highest level since May 15. At the time of writing, XAU/USD trades around $4,588, heading for a third consecutive weekly gain.

item.title: European gas: Storage gap supports high prices – Commerzbank
item.description: Norman Liebke at Commerzbank warns that low European gas storage, suspended LNG exports from Qatar and the end of the refilling phase are keeping European gas prices elevated.

item.title: Canada: Q2 GDP rebound faces future headwinds – RBC
item.description: Royal Bank of Canada economists Nathan Janzen and Abbey Xu expect Canadian gross domestic product data for June and Q2 to confirm a strong rebound after winter stagnation.

item.title: Euro pares gains against US Dollar but eyes fourth weekly advance
item.description: EUR/USD reverses its earlier gains on Friday as the US Dollar (USD) steadies after retesting the three-month low touched the previous day. At the time of writing, the pair trades around 1.1677, easing from an intraday high of 1.1711, its highest level since May 14.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Soft Dollar and BoJ outlook shift near-term tone – Scotiabank
item.description: Scotiabank strategists Shaun Osborne and Eric Theoret point out that Japan’s July Consumer Price Index (CPI) and stronger August Purchasing Managers' Index (PMI) data support expectations for Bank of Japan (BoJ) tightening, with about 20 bps of hikes priced in swaps.

item.title: Breaking: S&P Global Composite PMI is seen at 56 in August
item.description: US business activity is predicted to have gained momentum in August, according to the flash reading of S&P Global’s Composite PMI, which ticked up to 56 from 54.5 in July.

item.title: Gold: Upside asymmetry into next week – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities’ Ryan McKay and Bart Melek note that Gold and broader precious metals are trading in a higher range that could trigger another round of CTA (Commodity Trading Advisors) buying.

item.title: British Pound: Mixed data but Sterling supported – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s (BBH) Elias Haddad says GBP/USD is firmer on broad US Dollar (USD) weakness despite mixed United Kingdom (UK) data.

item.title: Canadian Dollar: Bullish structure points to 1.35 handle against US Dollar – Scotiabank
item.description: Scotiabank strategists Shaun Osborne and Eric Theoret note that the Canadian Dollar (CAD) continues to show strength against the US Dollar (USD).

item.title: Euro area: PMIs signal resilient growth – Nomura
item.description: Nomura’s European Economics team notes that Euro area August Purchasing Managers' Index (PMI) showed resilient growth, led by a strong manufacturing rebound, while price pressures eased.

item.title: Canadian Dollar heads for fourth weekly gain on weaker US Dollar, elevated Oil prices
item.description: USD/CAD extends its decline on Friday as broad US Dollar (USD) weakness and elevated Oil prices provide a double boost to the Canadian Dollar (CAD). At the time of writing, the pair trades around 1.3745, while the Loonie is on track for a fourth consecutive weekly gain.

item.title: Brent: Supply risks keep prices elevated – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Barbara Lambrecht says tensions around the Strait of Hormuz and tight diesel inventories continue to support Brent. With prices near USD 94 and almost 20% above their early-August lows, Brent remains well below its April peak.

item.title: WTI advances as supply tensions overshadow US inventory build
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI) US Oil trades around $86.50 on Friday at the time of writing, up 0.63% on the day. US Oil remains close to Thursday’s high of $87.38, its highest level in more than three weeks, as concerns about global energy supplies continue to support prices.

item.title: US Dollar: Bearish regime reinforced by bull flattener – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities strategists argue that the United States (US) Treasury buyback announcement has reinforced bearish momentum for the Dollar.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Support test as Japan data firm – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s (BBH) Elias Haddad highlights USD/JPY testing key support at its 200-day moving average as Japanese data firm.

item.title: Indonesia: Expansionary stance with narrowing buffer – Standard Chartered
item.description: Standard Chartered’s Aldian Taloputra assesses Indonesia’s 2027 fiscal plans, noting a targeted deficit of 2.4% of GDP versus 2.9% in 2026. The bank maintains its own forecast of a 2.9%-of-GDP deficit, citing ambitious revenue assumptions and potential tax shortfalls.

item.title: Gold: Safe-haven bid on US debt worries – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Carsten Fritsch notes Gold has surged, breaking above USD 4,500 per troy ounce as safe‑haven demand rises on US debt concerns and a weaker Dollar.

item.title: EUR/GBP Price Forecast: Neutral RSI signals further consolidation
item.description: EUR/GBP remains stuck in a narrow trading range this month, stalling the rebound from near 0.8460 in mid-July as buyers struggle to clear the 50-day Simple Moving Average (SMA).

item.title: British Pound dips hold above 216.50 Japanese Yen following mixed UK data
item.description: British Pound's (GBP) rally against the Japanese Yen (JPY) was capped at the 217.00 area earlier on Friday, and the pair pulled back to the 216.50 area where it found some support.

item.title: Canadian Dollar: Binary tariff risks shape near-term path – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities strategists argue that Section 338 tariff negotiations pose a binary risk for the Canadian Dollar (CAD) and USD/CAD.

item.title: Silver climbs toward $70 as US Dollar remains under pressure
item.description: Silver (XAG/USD) accelerates its advance on Friday and trades around $69.75 at the time of writing, up 2.41% on the day. The white metal reaches its highest level in two months and is on track for a weekly gain of more than 7%, mainly supported by persistent weakness in the US Dollar (USD).

item.title: Euro: Set to outperform Pound, US Dollar and Yen - Nomura
item.description: Nomura strategists see greater fiscal vulnerabilities in the United Kingdom (UK) than in the Euro area. Strong foreign inflows into Euro area bonds and comparatively better debt dynamics support its view that Euro (EUR) should outperform British Pound (GBP), US Dollar (USD) and Japanese Yen (JPY).

item.title: Indian Rupee remains under pressure amid elevated Oil prices
item.description: The Indian Rupee (INR) ticks lower against the US Dollar (USD) on Friday. The USD/INR edges up to near 95.72 as elevated oil prices have outweighed a weak US Dollar.

item.title: Australian Dollar rallies above 0.7150 as the US Dollar bleeds amid bond buybacks
item.description: The Australian Dollar (AUD) accelerated its rally against the US Dollar (USD) on Friday, hitting session highs above 0.7150 for the first time since early June and drawing closer to a three-month top, in the 0.7200 area.

item.title: Experts agree: Weak Dollar backs near-term upside in EUR/USD
item.description: The Euro (EUR) trades 0.21% higher at around 1.1710 against the US Dollar (USD) during the European trading session on Friday, the highest level seen in over three months.
